title: Matar Paneer (Peas and Cottage Cheese Curry)
description: Matar Paneer is a classic North Indian curry made with soft paneer cubes and green peas simmered in a rich, spiced tomato-onion gravy. It is comforting, flavorful, and pairs beautifully with naan, roti, or steamed basmati rice.

ingredients.title: For the Paneer and Peas
items: Paneer (cottage cheese) – 250 g, cut into 1-inch cubes
Green peas – 1 cup, fresh or frozen
Oil or ghee – 1–2 tsp for sautéing

ingredients.title: Spices
items: Red chili powder – 1 tsp (adjust to taste)
Kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) – ½ tsp

ingredients.title: Other
items: Fresh cream – ½ cup or yogurt – 2 tbsp (optional, for richness)
Fresh coriander leaves – chopped, for garnish

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing the Paneer and Peas
steps: Heat 1–2 tsp oil in a pan over medium heat.
Lightly sauté the paneer cubes until golden brown on all sides, if desired. Set aside.
Blanch fresh peas in boiling water for 2–3 minutes. Frozen peas can be added directly to the curry.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Making the Masala Base
steps: In the same pan, heat 2 tsp oil. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste and sauté for 1–2 minutes until the raw aroma disappears.
Add tomato puree, turmeric powder, red chili powder, coriander powder, and cumin powder.
Cook the masala until the oil separates from the mixture.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Cooking the Curry
steps: Add 1 cup water to the masala and stir to make a smooth gravy.
Add the peas and paneer cubes. Simmer for 5–7 minutes over low-medium heat.
Add garam masala and kasuri methi, then mix gently.
For a richer curry, stir in fresh cream or yogurt. Adjust the consistency with additional water if needed.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Garnishing and Serving
steps: Garnish with freshly chopped coriander leaves.
Serve hot with naan, roti, or steamed basmati rice.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot with naan or roti.
Pair with steamed basmati rice for a comforting meal.
Garnish lightly with fresh coriander leaves before serving.

chefTips: Use fresh, soft paneer for the best creamy texture.
Crush kasuri methi between your palms before adding it to release its aroma.
For extra depth of flavor, lightly roast the spices before adding them to the masala.
